confirmed.title: A plan run permanently deletes a flow's paused/failed interviews without ever telling the user
confirmed.scenario: Field used by an active flow that has paused or failed interviews on the versions that will go. Open All at once, leave the flow row on its default (Remove, or Replace with a replacement field picked; also Delete when chosen), press Run. The only place the interviews are named is the row's own confirmation (extraHtml '... that will be deleted first'), and the plan hook answers that dialog with true without drawing it because its items are 'Name vN'. fixFlowExecute then calls _deleteFlowInterviews. The plan screen never lists interviews (_planFlowNo reads only the preview) and says 'Every change keeps a restore point'; the interviews cannot be re-created and the undo note says so only afterwards. The comment on fcPlanOwnsDialog claims the paused interviews are 'asked as always' - that is true only for purgeOldFlowVersions' separate dialog (line 6190), not for the fixOne path the plan uses.
confirmed.why:
The claim survives; I found no guard.

- **The plan auto-answers the flow row's dialog.** `field-cleaner.js:1727` installs `sftkConfirmPlanned(opts => (_planRun && fcPlanOwnsDialog(opts, _planRun.name)) ? true : undefined)`. `sftk-confirm.js:26-28` returns that `true` before anything is drawn. `fcPlanOwnsDialog` (`field-cleaner.js:450-455`) looks only at `opts.items` labels.
- **The flow dialog's items always match.** In `fixOne` (`field-cleaner.js:5248-5250`) the items are `${componentName} v${v.num}` for every version in `shownPlan.toDelete` plus the overwrite. `componentName` is the `row.name` the plan passed at line 1751 and stored in `_planRun.name` at line 1746.
- **The interviews are named only inside that suppressed dialog.** They appear in `extraHtml` at `field-cleaner.js:5263` ("that will be deleted first"). They are not in `items`, so they have no effect on ownership. The required acknowledgement (`needsCheckbox`, line 5258) is skipped with the dialog.
- **The delete then runs.** `fixFlowExecute` at `field-cleaner.js:6046-6047` calls `_deleteFlowInterviews(fp.interviews, journal)`, which issues `SF_REST_DELETE` on `FlowInterview` (line 5668). The code's own comments say these cannot be re-created (lines 5670 and 6059).
- **The interviews exist whenever the scenario holds.** `fp.interviews` is read for `plan.toDelete` at `field-cleaner.js:5875`, so any paused or failed interview on a version that goes is included.
- **The plan screen never mentions them.** `_planFlowNo` (`field-cleaner.js:1595-1604`) reads only `fp.plan.mode`, `fp.planDelete` and `fp.preview`. `r.note` (lines 1663-1664) is set only for a missing remove way or a Leave pick. The plan header at line 1675 says "Runs without asking again. Every change keeps a restore point".
- **The default pick reaches this path.** `fcPlanDefault` (`field-cleaner.js:426-427`) picks replace or remove for a flow row, so pressing Run without touching the row triggers it.
- **The comments are wrong for this path.** The comment at lines 447-449 ("the flow's paused interviews ... asked as always") holds only for the separate dialog in `purgeOldFlowVersions` (`field-cleaner.js:6188-6199`), whose items are interview labels. The comment at line 5658 ("every caller confirms first") is not true under a plan run.

I did not run any test; this is from reading the code.
confirmed.fix:
Make the plan not own a dialog that deletes interviews.

1. In `fixOne`'s `sftkConfirmDestructive` call (`field-cleaner.js:5245`), add a flag for flows: `unrecoverable: type === 'Flow' && flowPlan.interviews.length > 0`.
2. In `fcPlanOwnsDialog` (`field-cleaner.js:450`), start with `if (opts && opts.unrecoverable) return false;`.

The hook then returns `undefined` for that row, so the row's own dialog is drawn mid-run, naming the interviews and requiring the acknowledgement. This is what the comment at lines 447-449 already promises. A cancel returns 'cancel' and the row is reported as not done.

Optionally, also have `_planFlowNo` (`field-cleaner.js:1595`) hand back `fp.interviews.length` so the plan line can carry a note such as "N paused/failed runs will be deleted — asked when it runs".

confirmed.title: A flow with no active version using the field is planned as '✂ Remove', picked by default, and its versions are deleted with no undo
confirmed.scenario: A flow whose referencing versions are all inactive (e.g. a deactivated or draft-only flow: every version names the field). Its row button is '🗑 Delete N old versions' with class btn-secondary, data-swap=0 and no data-way, so _planRows classes it as kind 'remove'. fcPlanDefault picks 'remove', the plan shows it under the '✂ Remove' button and counts it as 'removed'. On Run the row's confirmation (which normally needs the 'permanent' tick) is auto-answered; fixFlowExecute deletes every referencing version - for a draft-only/deactivated flow that is the whole flow - and returns undo: { none: ... 'a deleted flow version cannot be re-created' } because activeGone is false. The row gets a ↩ Undo button that only opens Activity, and ↩ Undo all does not count or restore it. CHANGELOG promises 'Flows, code and rules are never set to Delete by the tool' and 'Undo all takes everything back'; the plan screen promises '↩ Undo on each row afterwards'.
confirmed.why:
The claim survives; I found no guard on the path.

- **Row button** — `field-cleaner.js:1471-1472`: a flow card with no active referencing version gets one button, `btn-secondary`, `data-swap="0"`, no `data-way`, labelled "Delete N old versions".
- **Plan kind** — `field-cleaner.js:1586`: not swap, not `btn-danger`, way is not `off`, so the kind is `remove`.
- **Default pick** — `field-cleaner.js:426-427`: `fcPlanDefault` returns `remove` before it reaches the "automation is never picked for deletion" rule at 428-430. `planEverything` (1653-1658) only pre-reads flows with `way === 'keep'`, so this row is not filtered. It is drawn as "✂ Remove" and counted as "removed" (1619, 1643).
- **Confirmation bypassed** — `field-cleaner.js:5245-5258`: the row's own dialog has `needsCheckbox: true` for a flow and items labelled `${componentName} v${num}`. `fcPlanOwnsDialog` (450-454) matches exactly those labels, and `sftk-confirm.js:26-28` returns true without drawing the dialog. `wantBackup` is also false in a plan run (5182), so no zip is downloaded.
- **No undo** — `field-cleaner.js:6063-6086`: `activeGone` requires the active version to be in `toDelete` or `out.deactivated`. With no active referencing version it is false, so `out.undo = { none: ... }` is written to the journal at 5311.
- **Row afterwards** — `markFixed` (5405) still draws "↩ Undo". `undoRow` (5115-5117) finds no undoable entry and only opens Activity.

For a draft-only or deactivated flow where every version names the field, the whole flow is deleted. The metadata is kept as a restore point, but it can only be put back by hand as a draft.

This contradicts three promises:
- `CHANGELOG.md:21`: "Flows, code and rules are never set to Delete by the tool" and "Undo all takes everything back".
- `field-cleaner.js:1675` (plan screen): "↩ Undo on each row afterwards".
- `field-cleaner.js:1784` (report): "Every change has ↩ Undo on its row".

Nothing was run; this is from reading the code only.
confirmed.fix:
Classify the versions-only flow button as a delete so the plan never picks it by default.

1. `field-cleaner.js:1472`: add `data-way="versions"` to the button. `fixOne` (5100) maps unknown ways to `''`, so the row's own click behaves as before.
2. `field-cleaner.js:1586`: change the test to `(b.classList.contains('btn-danger') || b.dataset.way === 'off' || b.dataset.way === 'versions') ? 'delete' : 'remove'`.

`fcPlanDefault` then returns `leave` for the flow (it is not in the `plain` list). The row shows "🗑 Delete" in the plan and runs only if the owner picks it or presses "Delete what is left".

The catch: a flow whose active version is clean and only old versions name the field is also left for the owner, which is the conservative side.

The "↩ Undo on each row" wording (1675, 1784) stays inaccurate for any flow-version delete the owner does pick; rewording it is a separate, optional change.

confirmed.title: Aura application / event / interface / tokens bundle is written back with a .cmp-meta.xml file
confirmed.scenario: An Aura APPLICATION bundle MyApp names the field. _codeRead maps its definition to path 'MyApp.app'; sftkMdBundleFiles then builds the zip as package.xml, aura/MyApp/MyApp.app and aura/MyApp/MyApp.cmp-meta.xml. The Metadata API names an app's meta file MyApp.app-meta.xml (evt / intf / tokens likewise). This zip is both the Replace / Edit deploy and the restore point of a Delete. If Salesforce rejects the unpaired meta file (not checked live), Replace fails on every such bundle and, worse, Delete succeeds (destructive deploy) and Undo cannot put the bundle back. If it accepts it, the bundle's apiVersion and description are not carried. Reproduced the file list; the tests only cover a COMPONENT bundle.
confirmed.evidence:
738: const metaFile = lwc ? `${s.bundle}/${name}/${name}.js-meta.xml` : `${s.bundle}/${name}/${name}.cmp-meta.xml`;
field-cleaner.js 7124: const _AURA_FILE = { COMPONENT: n => `${n}.cmp`, APPLICATION: n => `${n}.app`, EVENT: n => `${n}.evt`, INTERFACE: n => `${n}.intf`, TOKENS: n => `${n}.tokens`, …
confirmed.why:
Not refuted on the code; the Salesforce outcome is unverified (no org touched), so the severity is open.

Code path, confirmed by reading:
- sftk-mdapi.js:738 hardcodes the Aura meta file: `const metaFile = lwc ? `${s.bundle}/${name}/${name}.js-meta.xml` : `${s.bundle}/${name}/${name}.cmp-meta.xml`;`. sftkMdBundleFiles (712-744) never sees the DefType, only `{ path, source }`.
- field-cleaner.js:7141 `_AURA_FILE` maps APPLICATION / EVENT / INTERFACE / TOKENS to `.app` / `.evt` / `.intf` / `.tokens`, and field-cleaner.js:9312 builds the resources from it, so an app bundle yields aura/MyApp/MyApp.app plus aura/MyApp/MyApp.cmp-meta.xml (9319 passes only path and source to sftkMdBundleFiles).
- No guard keeps non-component bundles out: the scan at field-cleaner.js:2680-2690 queries every AuraDefinition with no DefType filter and adds the bundle whenever any source names the field as a whole word. An .app markup or its controller naming the field is enough.
- The tests only pin a COMPONENT bundle: test/fc-delete-1107.test.mjs:77 and test/fc-matrix-code-1114.test.mjs:436 and 461. The live demo fixtures (scripts/dev/live/demo/live-fix4.mjs:43, live-fix5.mjs:25) are .cmp bundles too, so the app/evt/intf/tokens shape was never exercised.

What I could not settle: whether the Metadata API rejects an unpaired MyApp.cmp-meta.xml in an application bundle, ignores it (apiVersion and description then fall to defaults), or accepts any *-meta.xml as the bundle's meta (harmless). The documented name is MyApp.app-meta.xml, so the generated name is wrong by the docs in every case; only the first two outcomes hurt a user, and the first is the serious one (Replace fails; a Delete's restore point cannot redeploy).
confirmed.fix: In sftkMdBundleFiles (sftk-mdapi.js:738), derive the Aura meta name from the bundle's main resource instead of hardcoding .cmp: find the resource whose file name is `${name}.app`, `${name}.evt`, `${name}.intf`, `${name}.tokens` or `${name}.cmp` and use `${s.bundle}/${name}/${name}.${ext}-meta.xml`, falling back to `cmp` when none matches. Add a test for an APPLICATION bundle expecting aura/MyApp/MyApp.app-meta.xml.

confirmed.title: Search-layout edit on a custom object deploys <profileSearchLayouts> with its <fields> stripped
confirmed.scenario: Custom object Foo__c has a profile-specific search results layout: `<profileSearchLayouts><fields>A__c</fields><fields>B__c</fields><profileName>Admin</profileName></profileSearchLayouts>`. Remove or replace A__c in one search layout. For a custom object the deployed file is the whole object minus child components, and the child stripping drops every <fields> element at any depth, so the file carries `<profileSearchLayouts><profileName>Admin</profileName></profileSearchLayouts>` (reproduced). If Salesforce applies that as written (not checked live), the Admin profile's search-result columns are emptied. The Undo file is built by the same function (field-cleaner.js 6986, with a field name that matches nothing), so it is stripped the same way and does not restore them.
confirmed.why:
The stripping is real and nothing guards it; only the Salesforce-side effect is unverified (no org touched).

- sftk-mdapi.js:1069 `for (const t of CHILDREN) rest = _sftkMdWalk(rest, t, () => 'drop').xml;` with 'fields' in CHILDREN (1052).
- _sftkMdWalk (853-868) drops every element sftkMdFindElement returns, and sftkMdFindElement (102-132) is a regex scan for the first `<fields>` at or after the cursor at any nesting depth. It has no notion of top-level. Once the top-level `<fields>` are consumed, the next match is the `<fields>` inside `<profileSearchLayouts>`, which is dropped, leaving `<profileSearchLayouts><profileName>Admin</profileName></profileSearchLayouts>`.
- sftk-mdapi.js:1071 uses `rest` for any object matching /__c$/, so this file is what a custom object deploys.
- field-cleaner.js:6984-6988 passes the full readMetadata CustomObject innerXml straight in, with no filtering of profileSearchLayouts. A grep for `profileSearchLayouts` across the repo's js/mjs/md files returns nothing, so no code and no test knows the element exists.
- field-cleaner.js:7002 deploys `ed.file`. The verify at 7018-7024 only checks the edited tag through sftkSearchLayoutHits, which looks only inside `<searchLayouts>`, so the loss passes as verified.
- field-cleaner.js:7003-7004 builds the undo zip with the same function (`'__sftk_none__'`), so it goes through the same line 1069 strip and cannot put the profile columns back.

Not established: what Salesforce does with a `<profileSearchLayouts>` that has a profileName and no fields. It either empties that profile's search-result columns, with an undo that does not restore them, or rejects the deploy, so the edit fails on any custom object that has a profile-specific search layout. Both are user-visible. The precondition is ordinary: ProfileSearchLayouts is a documented CustomObject member, returned whenever an admin has set a per-profile search results layout.
confirmed.fix: In sftkSearchLayoutEdit (sftk-mdapi.js:1068-1069), keep `<profileSearchLayouts>` out of the child strip. Before the CHILDREN loop, walk `rest` for 'profileSearchLayouts', push each whole element to an array and replace it with a placeholder that contains no tags (e.g. `\u0000PSL<i>\u0000`). Run the CHILDREN loop, then substitute the saved elements back. The undo file is built by the same function, so it is fixed by the same change. Add a test with a Thing__c object carrying `<profileSearchLayouts><fields>A__c</fields><profileName>Admin</profileName></profileSearchLayouts>` asserting that `file` still contains it intact.

confirmed.title: A Toolkit change pushed past the 100-entry cap cannot be seen, undone, backed up or cleared anywhere
confirmed.scenario: The cap of 100 is shared by deployments and every tool. Run Field Cleaner 'All at once' on field A (60 components, 60 entries), then on field B (60 more). The first 20 entries of A go to IndexedDB. Pick field A again: the bar says 40 changes can be undone and Undo all takes back 40; the 20 oldest stay changed in the org. Their row Undo finds nothing and opens the tool window, which does not list them either. The popup never reads the archive (sftkHistoryAll returns the hot list only), and Data Studio's 'Show older' filters Toolkit entries out of the archived view. Back up omits them, and Clear all ('removes these entries from this browser') leaves them in IndexedDB, where Data Studio's 'Export all (incl. archive)' still writes them out with the earlier metadata state.
confirmed.evidence:
sftk-history.js 194-197: async function sftkHistoryAll() { if (_sftkHistStudio()) return _history; try { return (await chrome.storage.local.get('sftk_history')).sftk_history || []; } ...
sftk-history.js 189-191: split = sftkHistorySplit(list, SFTK_HISTORY_CAP) ... await sftkArchPut(split.overflow) ... set({ sftk_history: split.keep })
studio-history.js 467: const mineArch = _archShown.filter(r => typeof sftkHistoryToolTab !== 'function' || !sftkHistoryToolTab(r));
sftk-history.js 510-513 (ClearTab) and sftk-toolhistory.js 148 (backup) read only sftk_history.
confirmed.why:
Not refuted: no reader of the archive exists for Toolkit entries, and the project already hit this cap live.

- **Overflow goes to IndexedDB only.** `sftk-history.js:189-191` (popup) splits at `SFTK_HISTORY_CAP` = 100 (`:42`), sends the overflow to `sftkArchPut` and keeps the newest 100. `sftkHistorySplit` (`sftk-archive.js:21-26`) is a plain `slice(-100)` over one list shared by deployments, every tool and every undo entry. Data Studio does the same at `studio-core.js:673-675`.
- **Every Toolkit surface reads the hot list only.** `sftkHistoryAll` (`sftk-history.js:194-197`) returns `_history` or `sftk_history`. Its callers are the Undo-all bar (`field-cleaner.js:10151`), the row Undo (`field-cleaner.js:5116`, which opens the tool window at `:5117` when nothing is found), the tool window list (`sftk-toolhistory.js:44`), Back up (`sftk-toolhistory.js:148`) and the feed (`sftk-feed.js:154, 202`).
- **Nothing reads the archive for Toolkit entries.** The only readers are in `studio-history.js` (`sftkArchList` at `:1096` and `:1108`). The archived view drops Toolkit entries at `:467` (`!sftkHistoryToolTab(r)`), so "Show older" never lists them. `sftkHistoryUndo` (`sftk-history.js:314-316`) finds an archived entry only when the caller hands it in via `o.entry`, and no caller can obtain it.
- **Clear and single delete leave the archive alone.** `sftkHistoryClearTab` (`sftk-history.js:503-515`) and `sftkHistoryRemove` (`:518-533`) rewrite `sftk_history` / `_history` only; neither touches IndexedDB. The Clear tooltip says "Removes these entries from this browser" (`sftk-toolhistory.js:143`).
- **The archived entries still leave the machine.** "Export all (incl. archive)" (`studio-history.js:1108-1115`) writes every archived entry, Toolkit ones included, with their `toolUndo` earlier state.
- **The cap is reachable.** `docs/BACKLOG.md:110` (2026-11-17) records an Undo all of 39 that lost its two oldest targets because "Activity keeps 100 entries at hand, every undo adds one". The fix there (`o.entry`) only covers entries already held in memory by a running Undo all, not ones archived before the field is picked again. Field Cleaner writes one entry per component, so two 60-component runs reproduce the claim.

The only user-visible mention of the archive is the Restore message (`sftk-toolhistory.js:175`); no path leads to the archived Toolkit entries. I read the code only; nothing was run.
confirmed.fix:
Smallest change, two parts in `sftk-history.js` plus one helper in `sftk-archive.js`:

1. **Make `sftkHistoryAll` include archived Toolkit entries.** After reading the hot list, when `sftkArchList` is defined, append the archived entries for which `sftkHistoryToolTab(e)` is non-empty and whose id is not already in the hot list. The Undo-all bar, row Undo, tool window and Back up then see them, and `sftkHistoryUndo` finds them through `all.find`. The append must be a copy, never a push into Data Studio's `_history`.

2. **Make Clear and delete reach the archive.** Add `sftkArchDelete(ids)` to `sftk-archive.js` (a `store.delete` per id). Call it from `sftkHistoryClearTab` for archived entries where `sftkHistoryInTab(e, tab)`, and from `sftkHistoryRemove` for the one id, so "Removes these entries from this browser" holds and Export all no longer writes them.

One follow-on to handle: after undoing an archived entry, `sftkHistoryAppend(entry)` at `sftk-history.js:402` would push it back into the hot list. Write the `done` mark back with `sftkArchPut([entry])` instead when the entry came from the archive.

confirmed.title: Data Studio's 'Clear All' also deletes every Toolkit change and its Undo, which the page says are not listed there
confirmed.scenario: Data Studio > History shows the note 'N changes made with Toolkit tools are not listed here — each is in the tool that made it, with its Undo'. Press Clear All; the dialog asks only 'Delete all transfer history records?'. Confirming sets _history = [] and clears the archive, so all Field Cleaner, Flows, Licenses and other Toolkit entries are gone with their Undo, without being named or counted. The Toolkit's own Clear dialog says the opposite split: 'Deployments and their restore points stay — they are cleared in Data Studio > History'. This behaviour is also on master.
confirmed.why:
The claim survives; no guard was found.

- **The shared list holds both kinds.** `renderHistory` (studio-history.js:466) calls `sftkHistoryStudioSplit(_history)`, which only splits for display (sftk-history.js:584-590): Toolkit entries are counted into `kit`, not removed from `_history`.
- **Clear All wipes all of it.** The handler at studio-history.js:929-937 sets `_history = []`, clears the archive (which also holds overflowed Toolkit entries), then calls `storageSaveHistory()`.
- **The save does not bring them back.** `storageSaveHistory` (studio-core.js:658-678) re-reads storage with `_historyAdoptToolUpdates(_history, cur, false)`. With `addNew` false, ids missing locally are not re-added (studio-core.js:641), so `sftk_history` is written as `[]`.
- **The Undo goes with the entry.** A Toolkit change's earlier state is kept in the entry itself (sftk-toolhistory.js:193: "the earlier state is kept in the entry"), so deleting the entry deletes its Undo.
- **The user is never told.** The dialog says only "Delete all transfer history records?" (studio-history.js:926). The same page states the Toolkit changes "are not listed here — each is in the tool that made it, with its Undo" (studio-history.js:339). The Toolkit's own Clear dialog promises the opposite split (sftk-toolhistory.js:194).

Trigger: at least one Toolkit tool entry exists (Field Cleaner, Flows, etc.); open Data Studio > History, press Clear History, then Clear All. Every tool's Activity list is then empty and the Undo is unrecoverable unless it was backed up.

Not checked: I did not run it or diff against master; this is from reading the code on the branch.
confirmed.fix:
In the `dsConfirmClearHistory` handler (studio-history.js:931), keep the Toolkit entries instead of emptying the list: `_history = _history.filter(e => typeof sftkHistoryToolTab === 'function' && sftkHistoryToolTab(e));`

The archive needs the same treatment, because `sftkArchClear()` on line 933 also drops archived Toolkit entries. Either delete only non-Toolkit archived entries, or read the archived Toolkit entries first and put them back with `sftkArchPut` after the clear.

`sftkUndoStoreClear` and `sftkFcSweep` can stay as they are: they hold deployment restore points and per-run before/after lists, while a Toolkit Undo lives in its entry.

Alternative if wiping everything is intended: make the dialog say so, naming the count of Toolkit changes and that their Undo goes too, and correct the wording at sftk-toolhistory.js:194.

confirmed.title: A second run in the same page session PATCHes a rule's cached, stale Metadata and reverts edits made to the rule in between
confirmed.scenario: Open a deployment's Deploy page, tick validation rule R, run (run 1). Without reloading Data Studio, edit R in Setup (formula, message, error field), for example to fix what run 1 tripped on. Run again with R ticked. _depRulePause.list is never re-read for the same target and object set, and sftkVrPauseHydrate skips a rule that already carries metadata from run 1. The switch-off PATCH and the switch-back PATCH both send run 1's whole Metadata with only active changed, so R silently goes back to its old formula and message. The History undo step carries the same old body. This breaks the rule that only active changes.
confirmed.evidence:
studio-deploy.js 2372: `if (!_depRulePause.on || _depRulePause.key !== key) load(); else paint();` (the only place the list is assigned is load())
studio-deploy.js 2429: `try { await sftkVrPauseHydrate(sess, vp.rules); }` (vp.rules are the same objects as _depRulePause.list.rules; sftkPauseKeep pushes x itself)
sftk-vrpause.js 96: `if (r.metadata || r.xml) continue;`
sftk-vrpause.js 163-165: `const md = ... sftkMetaForPatch(rule.metadata || {}) ...; return { Metadata: { ...md, active: !!active } };`
confirmed.why:
The claim survives; I found no guard that forces a fresh read on a second run.

- **The list is loaded once per target and object set.** `studio-deploy.js:2372` is `if (!_depRulePause.on || _depRulePause.key !== key) load(); else paint();`. A grep for assignments shows `_depRulePause` and its `.list` are only set inside `load()` (2356, 2363). Nothing resets `on`, `key` or `list` after a run, so re-rendering the Deploy page with the same target and objects only repaints.
- **The run mutates the cached objects.** `sftkPauseKeep` (`sftk-pausepanel.js:74-83`) pushes the list items themselves (`(sk.has(...) ? kept : act).push(x)`). `_depReconcile` passes them as `vp.rules` (2413-2414) to `sftkVrPauseHydrate` (2429), which sets `r.metadata = rec.Metadata` (`sftk-vrpause.js:100`) or `r.xml` (97) on those cached objects.
- **Run 2 skips the read.** `sftk-vrpause.js:96` is `if (r.metadata || r.xml) continue;`, so the definition from run 1 is reused.
- **The stale body is what gets written.** `_sftkVpBody` (163-165) sends `{ Metadata: { ...sftkMetaForPatch(rule.metadata), active } }`, the whole of run 1's Metadata. The switch-off PATCH (via 2435), the switch-back in `sftkVrPauseOn` (which also skips rules that carry metadata, line 235) and the History undo step (`_sftkVpWriteMsg(x, true)`, line 215) all use it.
- **Packaged rules have the same problem.** `sftkVrPausePkgFiles` deploys the cached `rule.xml`.
- **The verify does not catch it.** The re-read in `_sftkVpSwitch` checks only `Active`, so the reverted formula and message pass silently.

The rule is still active after run 1 switches it back on, so it stays in the cached list with the same Id and the scenario needs nothing unusual. Not run live; this is from reading the code only.
confirmed.fix:
In `_depReconcile`'s `beforeWrites` (`studio-deploy.js`, just before line 2429), drop the cached definitions so every run reads them fresh:

`for (const r of vp.rules) { delete r.metadata; delete r.xml; }`
`try { await sftkVrPauseHydrate(sess, vp.rules); }`

Removing the `if (r.metadata || r.xml) continue;` skip at `sftk-vrpause.js:96` has the same effect, since line 2429 is the only caller of `sftkVrPauseHydrate`. The skip in `sftkVrPauseOn` (line 235) can stay: it then reuses the definition read at the start of the same run.

confirmed.title: Suggest PII from a child record's editor replaces the saved deployment with the child-rooted view
confirmed.scenario: Saved deployment Account > Contact. On the Deploy page open the Contact list (a non-root object), open one record (▸ record, or compare > Edit values), click '🎭 Suggest PII for this record', tick one field, Apply. The editor was given the child VIEW of the deployment ({...p, tree: node, lastScan: s}) and passes it to _depPiiSuggest, which, once the policy changed, puts that object into _profiles and saves. The stored deployment now has the Contact node as its tree and the child scan as lastScan: the root object and every sibling branch are gone from storage. If the deployment had no piiPolicy yet, the new policy and salt also land only on the view.
confirmed.why:
The claim holds; I found no guard on the path.

confirmed.title: 🎭 inside Fields & mapping now replaces the mapping window; first-time per-target exceptions are dropped

The claim survives; no guard found.

The ⚙ Done handler (lines 342-350) writes only into that local. The only place it is attached to the node is line 559, inside the `#dsFmSave` click handler (546-573), which can no longer be clicked. First-time per-target exceptions are therefore lost.
- Row edits go to `mappings`, a live reference to `node.fieldMappings` (lines 10-11), so they stay in memory, but the Apply normalisation, `node.fieldMappingOrgs` (line 562) and `commitEditingProfile()` (line 573) never run.
- The path is reachable in the shipping build: studio-builder.js:1569 calls `bldPiiDecorateMappingModal` after `openFieldMappingModal` whenever `sftkShips('pii')`, and line 2270 wires the delegated click on `#dsModalBox`.

confirmed.fix:
Smallest fix that keeps the chooser: return to the mapping window when the chooser closes, and stop the exceptions living in a detached local.

1. studio-builder-modals.js:14 — attach the object up front so ⚙ edits are on the node like `mappings` are: `const overrides = node.fieldMappingOverrides || (node.fieldMappingOverrides = {});`. The existing Apply code at 559-560 still deletes it when empty; a mapping window closed without Apply would leave an empty `{}` on the node, so either tolerate that or delete it on the reopen path when empty.

2. studio-builder.js — keep `pathStr` in `_bldPiiModalCtx` (set in `bldPiiDecorateMappingModal`, line 2267) and give `bldOpenPiiFieldModal` an optional `onClose` callback. From `bldPiiMaskBtnClick` pass a callback that runs `openFieldMappingModal(ctx.pathStr).then(() => bldPiiDecorateMappingModal(ctx.pathStr))`. confirmed.title: Dry run whose poison record is accepted deletes pre-existing target records that an upsert node merely updated
confirmed.scenario: Target org where the poison (an Account with no Name) does not fail, e.g. a before-insert trigger or before-save flow that fills Account.Name when blank. Dry run of a deployment whose node uses an external-id upsert (PATCH composite/sobjects/<Obj>/<ExtId>) and whose rows match existing target records. The composite commits (nothing failed), every row answers success:true with a real id, and sftkProbeParseRound pushes all of them to `persisted` without looking at `created`. The check at lines 3176-3187 then re-reads those ids, finds them (they existed before the dry run) and calls sfCollectionsDelete on them. Existing target records are sent to the Recycle Bin, reported as "record(s) from the dry run WERE written ... deleted again", and the field values the upsert overwrote are not restored.
confirmed.why:
The claim survives; I found no guard.

- **Upsert nodes do reach the dry run.** `background.js:2523` pushes the sub with `upsertField: useUpsert ? upsertField : null`, and `sftkProbeCompositeBody` (`background.js:1277-1282`) sends it as `PATCH composite/sobjects/<Obj>/<ExtId>`. Rows that match existing target records are not filtered out before sending.
- **The parser never looks at `created`.** `background.js:1309-1310` is `if (x.success) { if (x.id && !/^@/.test(String(x.id))) out.persisted.push({ objType: s.objType, id: x.id, srcId }); ... }`. A Collections upsert row that only updated an existing record answers `success:true, created:false` with the pre-existing record's real id, so it lands in `persisted`.
- **The persisted check deletes whatever it finds.** `background.js:3175-3187` re-reads the ids with `SELECT Id FROM <o> WHERE Id IN (...)` and calls `sfCollectionsDelete(tgtOrgUrl, tgtSid, found)` on every id found. Nothing there distinguishes a record the dry run created from one that existed before, and nothing restores the fields the committed upsert overwrote.
- **The trigger condition is one the code itself anticipates.** `background.js:3152` and `1327-1328` handle "the poison record was ACCEPTED". The poison is an Account with only `Description` (`background.js:1252-1254`). For API inserts Salesforce checks required fields after before-insert triggers and before-save flows, so an org that fills a blank `Account.Name` there accepts it and the `allOrNone` composite commits.

In the normal case (poison fails) the other subrequests answer `PROCESSING_HALTED` or rolled-back errors, so `persisted` stays empty; the defect needs the accepted-poison precondition. This is from reading the code only; no test was run and no org was touched.

When it does trigger, pre-existing target records go to the Recycle Bin, are reported as "from the dry run WERE written ... deleted again", and keep the overwritten values if undeleted.
confirmed.fix:
In `sftkProbeParseRound` (`background.js:1310`), do not treat an upsert update as a dry-run-created record: `if (x.id && !/^@/.test(String(x.id)) && !(s.upsertField && x.created !== true)) out.persisted.push(...)`.

Optionally collect the updated ids (`s.upsertField && x.created === false`) into a separate list. After the loop at `background.js:3175`, push an error naming them: "N existing <Obj> record(s) were UPDATED by a dry-run round that did not roll back — not deleted; review them". That way the user is told about the overwrite and `sfCollectionsDelete` is never called on those ids.

confirmed.title: Exported CSV cells that begin with = + - @ are written as-is
confirmed.scenario: The 'text' column is a raw line of org content. An email template or custom label line '=HYPERLINK("http://x","y") {!Account.Status__c}' written by any template author lands in the admin's CSV as a live formula (reproduced: the cell is only quote-wrapped). The everyday case is an Apex continuation line "+ ',Status__c FROM Account';", which Excel shows as #NAME? instead of the code. cell() escapes quotes, commas and newlines only.
confirmed.evidence: const cell = v => { const s = String(v == null ? '' : v); return /[",\r\n]/.test(s) ? '"' + s.replace(/"/g, '""') + '"' : s; };
confirmed.why:
The claim holds; I found no guard anywhere on the path.

- `sftk-sweep.js:701` — `cell()` only quote-wraps when the value contains `"`, `,`, CR or LF. It never looks at the first character.
- `sftk-sweep.js:705` — the `text` column is `String(l.text || '').trim()`, pushed straight into the row.
- `sftk-sweep.js:46` — `l.text` is the raw matching metadata line: `line.replace(/\r$/, '').trim().slice(0, 300)`. The trim removes the indentation, so an indented Apex continuation line such as `+ ',Status__c FROM Account';` starts with `+` in the cell.
- `field-cleaner.js:3855-3861` — the only caller puts the string into a Blob with a BOM and downloads it as `.csv`. There is no sanitising in between.

A grep of the repo's JS for a formula-prefix neutraliser (`csvSafe`, `csvCell`, a `^[=+` pattern) found none.

So any swept line that names the field and starts with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` after trimming opens in Excel as a formula. The everyday result is `#NAME?` or a formula-error prompt instead of the code (Apex string concatenation, a `- ` list item in a label or doc, an `@AuraEnabled`/`@track` line, an `=`-led template line). The injection case is an `=HYPERLINK(...)` line written by a template or label author. The `component`, `section` and `path` columns are org-supplied too and take the same path.

Not run: this is from reading the code; I did not execute the export.
confirmed.fix:
In `cell()` at `sftk-sweep.js:701`, prefix a single quote when the value starts with a formula trigger, then apply the existing quoting:

`const cell = v => { let s = String(v == null ? '' : v); if (/^[=+\-@\t\r]/.test(s)) s = "'" + s; return /[",\r\n]/.test(s) ? '"' + s.replace(/"/g, '""') + '"' : s; };`

This covers every column. The `line` column is a positive integer, so it is unaffected. If `test/` has a sweep CSV test asserting exact cell text for such a line, it will need the new expectation.

confirmed.title: Flow Access and Copy Permissions re-send a write to ANOTHER org after SESSION_EXPIRED (the fix lightning-pages.js got in 1.1 was not applied here)
confirmed.scenario: Toolkit popped out as a tab on sandbox acme--uat.sandbox.my.salesforce.com; the sandbox tab is closed (or its session ended) while a production tab acme.my.salesforce.com is open. User clicks Copy (user-copy.js) or Assign (flow-permissions.js:131, same code). The background's same-org retry fails, the module wrapper then calls GET_SF_SESSION, and background getSfSession falls back to 'same base domain' (last 3 labels = my.salesforce.com) or 'any org tab' and returns PRODUCTION's session. The wrapper sets _orgUrl/_sid to production and re-sends the same message there. User, Profile, PermissionSet and FlowDefinition Ids are identical in a sandbox and its production, so PATCH User/{id} {ProfileId}, POST PermissionSetAssignment and the SetupEntityAccess insert succeed in production. The production gate was evaluated for the sandbox before the run, the History journal carries the sandbox orgUrl (Undo aims at the wrong org), and every later read/write of the tool silently stays on production. lightning-pages.js was pinned with lpSessionRetryOk on 2026-11-14 for exactly this; popup.js sendBg has freshIsCorrectOrg; these two wrappers have neither.

confirmed.why:
The claim survives; I found no guard.

**The wrappers accept any session.** `user-copy.js:1616-1625` and `flow-permissions.js:130-139` are the same code: on `SESSION_EXPIRED` they call `GET_SF_SESSION` with `activeTabUrl: _orgUrl`, and if `fresh.sid && fresh.orgUrl` they overwrite the module's `_orgUrl`/`_sid` and re-send `{ ...msg, orgUrl: fresh.orgUrl, sid: fresh.sid }`. There is no org comparison and no check that the sid differs.

**The background does not protect them.** `background.js:3766-3772` retries same-org only (`sftkOrgKey` equality plus a different sid), then rethrows `SESSION_EXPIRED` to the page. The `GET_SF_SESSION` case at `background.js:3863` returns `getSfSession()` unvalidated.

**`getSfSession` does fall through to production** (`background.js:6181-6209`) when no sandbox tab is open:
- Exact hostname match fails.
- Slug match `t.url?.includes('acme--uat')` fails against `acme.my.salesforce.com`.
- "Last-resort: same base domain" at 6197-6203 computes `my.salesforce.com` from `acme--uat.sandbox.my.salesforce.com`, and the production hostname ends with it.
- Failing that, line 6208 takes any org tab.
- It then returns `{ sid, orgUrl: apiOrigin }` for production (6282).

**The writes go through these wrappers directly:**
- `user-copy.js:1269`, `1292`, `1422`: `SF_PATCH`
- `user-copy.js:1318`, `1355`, `1388`: `SF_REST_POST`
- `flow-permissions.js:712`: `SF_COLLECTIONS_CREATE`

**It is worse than the claim states.** Every read at `user-copy.js:1274-1427` uses the same `bg()`. The first expired read already flips `_orgUrl`/`_sid` to production, so all later writes carry production's URL and sid without any retry being involved.

**The existing fix is not applied here.** `lightning-pages.js:3869` gates the retry with `lpSessionRetryOk` (4622-4627: same `sftkOrgKey`, sid differs from the failed one). `popup.js:4347-4350` has `freshIsCorrectOrg`. Neither wrapper in these two files has an equivalent.

**Preconditions:** the sandbox session is dead, no tab of the sandbox is open (neither `my.salesforce.com` nor `lightning.force.com`), and another org's tab is open. The Ids match only for records that existed at the last sandbox refresh; that part is Salesforce behaviour I did not test, and no org was touched.
confirmed.fix:
Gate both retries the way `lightning-pages.js:3869` does. `sftkOrgKey` is already global in the page: `sftk-org-identity.js` loads at `popup.html:360`, before `user-copy.js` (374) and `flow-permissions.js` (376).

In `user-copy.js:1618` and `flow-permissions.js:132`, replace `if (fresh?.sid && fresh?.orgUrl) {` with:

```js
const failedSid = msg.sid !== undefined ? msg.sid : _sid;
if (fresh?.sid && fresh?.orgUrl && sftkOrgKey(fresh.orgUrl) === sftkOrgKey(_orgUrl) && fresh.sid !== failedSid) {
```

Otherwise the wrapper falls through to `return resp;`, so the caller sees `SESSION_EXPIRED` and `_orgUrl`/`_sid` are left untouched.

confirmed.title: A plan run switches a validation rule off (or rewrites its formula) under the label '✂ Remove' with the choice dialog never shown
confirmed.scenario: An active validation rule in which every condition of the formula uses the field. sftkMdEditField does not refuse (it returns off=true, suggested=false), so _preflight leaves ✂ Remove enabled and the plan picks 'remove' by default. On Run, fixEdit builds the three-way dialog (remove conditions / switch off / edit myself) with vrMode preset to 'off', the plan hook answers it true without drawing it, and the rule is deployed with <active>false</active>. The plan screen showed only '✂ Remove' (button title: 'Take the field out of this ... refused, with the reason, when what is left would not work') and counted it as 'removed'. Same mechanism when ed.suggested is true: the formula is rewritten with the field's conditions dropped ('it changes when the rule fires') without the diff ever being shown. Undo exists, but the user confirmed a removal, not a deactivation of a rule guarding data.
confirmed.why:
The claim survives; I found no guard between the plan and the deploy.

- **Plan row gets ✂ Remove.** `field-cleaner.js:1505` draws ✂ Remove whenever `ways.remove && !_preWhy(id)`. `_preflight` (`field-cleaner.js:8645`) only records a reason when `ed.refused` is set.
- **The all-conditions case is not a refusal.** `sftk-mdapi.js:1244-1249` sets `<active>false</active>`, `off = true` and pushes a `how` line, with no `refuse()`. The operand case (`sftk-mdapi.js:1236-1242`) sets `suggested = true`, also with no refusal.
- **The plan defaults to remove.** `_planRows` (`field-cleaner.js:1585-1588`) maps the button to kind `remove`, and `fcPlanDefault` (`field-cleaner.js:427`) picks `remove` when it is offered. The plan line shows only "✂ Remove" (`field-cleaner.js:1619-1620`) and the summary chip counts it as "removed" (`field-cleaner.js:1643`).
- **The run reaches the three-way dialog code.** `_planExecute` calls `fixOne` (`field-cleaner.js:1751`), which calls `fixEdit` (`field-cleaner.js:5134`). For a non-swap `ValidationRule`, `vrChoice` is true (`field-cleaner.js:7508`) and `vrMode` is preset to `ed.suggested ? 'remove' : 'off'` (`field-cleaner.js:7510`).
- **The dialog is answered without being drawn.** `fixEdit` calls `sftkConfirmDestructive` with `items: [{ label: componentName }]` (`field-cleaner.js:7527`). `componentName` is the plan's `row.name`, so `fcPlanOwnsDialog` (`field-cleaner.js:450-454`) returns true. The hook at `field-cleaner.js:1727` returns true, and `sftk-confirm.js:26-28` resolves before any rendering, so `onRender` and the radio group never exist.
- **The preset is deployed.** `vrMode` keeps its preset, and `field-cleaner.js:7561` picks `vrOffXml` (rule deactivated) or `ed.xml` (formula rewritten with the field's conditions dropped). `fixEdit` has no `_planRun` check; the only one in the file is the flow backup at `field-cleaner.js:5182`.

The dialog's own text says "Choose what happens to the rule" and "Read the formula that is left — it changes when the rule fires" (`field-cleaner.js:7520`, `7530`), and that choice is skipped. The plan screen's "Runs without asking again" (`field-cleaner.js:1675`) never says a rule will be switched off.

What limits the damage: a restore point is taken, Undo verifies `<active>true</active>` (`field-cleaner.js:7572`), and the row afterwards reads "Switched off" (`field-cleaner.js:7616`). The user learns of it only after the deploy.

One detail of the claim is wrong but does not change the outcome: the plan button's tooltip is `o.label`, the button text "✂ Remove" (`field-cleaner.js:1588`, `1620`), not the long row title quoted in the claim.

Not run: this is from reading the code only; no test was executed.
confirmed.fix:
Make the validation-rule choice dialog one the plan never answers.

1. In `fixEdit`, add a flag to the `sftkConfirmDestructive` options at `field-cleaner.js:7524`: `planAsk: vrChoice`.
2. In the plan hook at `field-cleaner.js:1727`, let that dialog open as always: `sftkConfirmPlanned(opts => (_planRun && !opts.planAsk && fcPlanOwnsDialog(opts, _planRun.name)) ? true : undefined);`

The three-way dialog (remove conditions / switch off / edit myself) is then drawn during the run for each active validation rule. Cancel already returns `'cancel'` and leaves the row untouched.

Optionally, in `planEverything` (`field-cleaner.js:1660-1665`), set `r.note = 'asks during the run: remove conditions, switch off, or edit'` for `r.type === 'ValidationRule'` rows whose pick is `remove`, so the plan screen says the run will stop to ask.

confirmed.title: Replace in rule-entry, workflow, approval and field-update formulas ignores 'cannot tell' paths and reports a half edit as verified

confirmed.why:
The claim survives; I found no guard.

**Rule entries (AssignmentRule / AutoResponseRule / EscalationRule)**
- `field-cleaner.js:7431-7434` (`_mdReadOneRaw`) hands the edit the container child's innerXml, whose `<fullName>` is the short name with no dot. So `sftk-mdapi.js:1164` sets `host = null`.
- In `_sftkMdSwapToken` (`sftk-mdapi.js:893`), `ctx` falls back to objApi and `known` is false. A bare `Region__c` is therefore 'this' (line 902, n++).
- `Parent.Region__c` goes to `sftkRelHop(null, 'parent')`, which returns `{obj: null, kind: 'host'}` (`sftk-relmap.js:60`). That is counted in `rel` and never swapped (`sftk-mdapi.js:930`).
- `sftk-mdapi.js:1426-1433` reads only `f.n` and `c.n`: `hits += c.n + f.n; ... return { body: c.xml }`. `f.rel` is never tested, so the half-renamed formula is returned as changed with "rule entries: 1 reference now New__c".

**The verify passes on the half edit**
- `field-cleaner.js:7616` requires `!_editStillNames(type, after, field) && _editStillNames(type, after, nf)`.
- Probing `Parent.Region__c = "x" && New__c = "y"` for the old field gives n=0, rel=1, hits=0, so line 1437 issues a plain `refuse('no rule entry names the field')` with no `unsure`. `_editStillNames` (7466) returns false.
- Probing for `New__c` gives n=1, so true. `ok` is true and line 7636 prints "Replaced ... verified by re-reading the org".
- Parent on Case is Case, so the rule still names Case.Region__c and still blocks the delete.

**The other three kinds**
- WorkflowRule / SharingCriteriaRule (1354-1369), ApprovalProcess entryCriteria (1446-1453) and WorkflowFieldUpdate (1338-1349) also never read `f.rel`.
- There `host` is known, so `Parent.` resolves. The trigger is instead a custom lookup (`Lookup__r.Region__c`, kind 'custom', `sftk-relmap.js:68`) or What/Who beside a bare `Region__c`.
- This is narrower: it is a real miss only when that lookup actually reaches the picked object.

**Sibling kinds do guard**
- ValidationRule 1216, CustomField 1258 and WebLink / RestrictionRule 1308 all do `if (f.rel) { cannotTell(relWhy(f.kind)); break; }`.

This is from reading the code only; I did not run a test.
confirmed.fix:
In `sftkMdEditField` (`sftk-mdapi.js`), refuse as unsure whenever a formula has `rel`, as ValidationRule does at line 1216.

1. **Rule entries (1424-1435):** add `let relKind = null;` beside the other flags. Inside the walk, straight after `const f = formulas(body, 'formula');`, add `if (f.rel) { relKind = relKind || f.kind || 'custom'; return 'keep'; }`. After the walk, before the `formulaCut` test, add `if (relKind) { cannotTell(relWhy(relKind)); break; }`.
2. **ApprovalProcess (1444-1453):** the same three lines, with the `cannotTell` placed before the `apCut` / `formulaCut` refusals.
3. **WorkflowRule / SharingCriteriaRule (after 1354):** add `if (f.rel) { cannotTell(relWhy(f.kind)); break; }`.
4. **WorkflowFieldUpdate (after 1338):** add the same line.

Each `f.rel` test must come before any plain `refuse(...)` in its case: `cannotTell` only sets `unsure` when nothing has refused yet. With that, `_editStillNames` reads these as still naming the field.

confirmed.scenario: Pick the lookup Account.Partner__c, replacement New_Partner__c (sftkFieldReplaceCompat allows two lookups to the same object). - **Flows:** `sftk-fieldreplace.js:164-166` compares every segment with `oldL` (`partner__c`). `$Record.Partner__r.Name` adds nothing to `left`/`skipped`, while `$Record.Partner__c` is swapped at line 173.
- **No relationship-name handling anywhere:** a grep for `relationshipName` and `__r` in `field-cleaner.js`, `sftk-fieldreplace.js` and `sftk-mdapi.js` shows the only use is `field-cleaner.js:5865`, which resolves a hop's target object. Nothing derives the old lookup's own relationship name (`Partner__r`).
- **The picker allows the scenario:** `sftkFieldReplaceCompat` (`sftk-fieldreplace.js:42-45`) explicitly accepts two lookups with the same `referenceTo`, and `field-cleaner.js:1883-1887` offers them.

confirmed.fix:
When the old field's describe has `type === 'reference'` and a `relationshipName`, pass that name into the three replacers: `_sftkMdSwapToken` / `sftkMdEditXml` formulas, `sftkMdCodeReplace` (and the `stillNames` check at `field-cleaner.js:9408`), and `sftkFlowReplaceField`.

In each, test the text for the whole token `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_$])<relationshipName>(?![A-Za-z0-9_])`. If it is present, do not report done:
- Formulas: count it as `rel` with a new kind (e.g. `'ownrel'`) so `sftkMdEditXml` goes through `cannotTell` with a reason like "also reaches through Partner__r — edit it in Setup".
- Flows: in `sftk-fieldreplace.js:166`, also push `{ why: 'unknown' }` when a non-last segment equals the old relationship name, and let a string containing only the relationship name past the `includes(oldL)` early return at line 159.
- Code: make `stillNames` true (or refuse the replace) when the relationship token remains.

A fuller alternative is to also rename `Old__r` to the replacement field's `relationshipName` when the path in front of it resolves to this object. The refusal is the smallest safe change.

confirmed.title: A failed undo attempt closes the Undo for good; a connection drop during Undo all burns every remaining change
confirmed.scenario: Field Cleaner > Undo all on 39 changes; after the 5th the network drops or the session id expires (a session is still listed, so the 'Log in to' stop does not fire). Each of the remaining 34 entries runs, every step is refused, and each entry is still stamped toolUndo.done = { ok: false }. sftkToolUndoState then returns disabled 'Undo attempted' for all of them, sftkHistoryUndoableFor filters them out, and no path re-runs the steps even though nothing was written and the earlier state is still in the entry. Same for a single Undo whose only step is refused once (API limit, lock, validation error since fixed). Flow switches, Licenses, Copy Permissions and Flow Access have no restore-point fallback. A data rollback, by contrast, stays available after a failed attempt.
confirmed.why:
The claim survives; I found no guard, caller or reset that prevents it.

- **The stamp is unconditional.** `sftk-history.js:399-402` computes `okAll` and then sets `entry.toolUndo.done = { at, ok: okAll, entryId }` and persists it with `sftkHistoryAppend(entry)`, whatever the steps returned. This includes the case where every step was refused and nothing was written. Even a step skipped as "not logged in to <step.orgUrl>" (line 348) is noted `ok: false` and leads to the same stamp.
- **The stamp closes the Undo.** `sftkToolUndoState` (`sftk-history.js:204-207`) returns `disabled: true` with the label "Undo attempted" for any `u.done`, before it looks at `u.steps`. `sftkHistoryUndo` line 318 refuses a disabled entry, and `sftkHistoryUndoableFor` line 423 filters it out.
- **Nothing ever clears it.** A grep for `toolUndo.done` across the repo finds one writer (line 401) and only readers elsewhere (`sftk-history.js:611`, `sftk-toolhistory.js:67`, `studio-history.js:983`, `studio-core.js:643-644`). The `studio-core.js` merge only propagates the done state.
- **Undo all keeps going after failures.** `sftkHistoryUndoMany` (`sftk-history.js:448`) stops only when the result has no `r.entry` and the text matches `/^Log in to /`, which is the no-session return at line 322. With a session still listed but the network down or the sid rejected, each `send` returns `{ error }`, the write is refused, and the function returns with `entry` set. The loop then continues through every remaining entry and stamps each one.

I did not run the existing tests or check whether a test pins the current stamping behaviour.
confirmed.fix:
In `sftkHistoryUndo` (`sftk-history.js:401-402`), stamp `done` only when the undo actually changed the org:

`if (stepsRun.some(x => x.accepted)) { entry.toolUndo.done = { at: j.completedAt, ok: okAll, entryId: j.id }; await sftkHistoryAppend(entry); }`

When no step was accepted, the entry keeps its steps and stays undoable; the failed attempt is still recorded as its own Activity entry.

Optionally, in `sftkHistoryUndoMany`, also set `out.stopped` and break when a result has `r.entry` but its `undoEntry` has no accepted step, so a dropped connection does not grind through the remaining entries.

confirmed.title: Restore a backup says 'each with its Undo' while the oldest entries go straight to an archive nothing can read
confirmed.scenario: Back up 150 Toolkit changes on one browser (or over time), then Restore a backup on another browser, or on one whose list already holds 60 entries. The merge sorts by startedAt and keeps the newest 100; the rest is put in IndexedDB. The message reads 'Restored 150 changes ... each with its Undo · the 50 oldest went to the archive', but no screen lists an archived Toolkit entry (see the previous finding), so those 50 have no Undo. A second restore of the same file does not skip them (only hot ids are checked) and reports them as restored again. The archive write is also in a swallowed try/catch, so if IndexedDB fails the overflow is dropped while the message still says it went to the archive.
confirmed.evidence:
sftk-history.js 578-581: const split = ... sftkHistorySplit(m.list, SFTK_HISTORY_CAP) ...; if (split.overflow.length && typeof sftkArchPut === 'function') { try { await sftkArchPut(split.overflow); } catch (_) {} } await chrome.storage.local.set({ sftk_history: split.keep }); return { added: m.added, skipped: m.skipped, archived: split.overflow.length };
sftk-toolhistory.js 172-175: `⬆ Restored ${n} change(s) from ${f.name}, each with its Undo` ... ` · the ${res.archived} oldest went to the archive: the list keeps ${SFTK_HISTORY_CAP}`
confirmed.why:
The claim survives; no guard was found.

**The overflow path is real.** In the popup (non-Studio) path, `sftk-history.js:576-581` merges the backup into the hot list, sorts by `startedAt`, and calls `sftkHistorySplit(m.list, SFTK_HISTORY_CAP)` with the cap at 100 (`sftk-history.js:42`). The overflow goes to `sftkArchPut` inside `try { ... } catch (_) {}`, and the function returns `archived: split.overflow.length` whether or not the put succeeded.

**Nothing reads an archived Toolkit entry back.**
- `sftkHistoryAll` (`sftk-history.js:194-197`) reads only `chrome.storage.local.sftk_history`.
- `sftkHistoryUndo` (`sftk-history.js:314-316`) looks only in that list, or in an entry the caller hands in, and otherwise returns "This entry is no longer in Activity."
- `sftk-toolhistory.js` mentions the archive only in the restore message at line 175.
- The one archive reader is `sftkArchList` in `studio-history.js:1096`, and `studio-history.js:467` filters Toolkit entries out of what it shows: `_archShown.filter(r => ... !sftkHistoryToolTab(r))`.

**The message overstates.** `sftk-toolhistory.js:172-175` prints "Restored N changes ..., each with its Undo" with N = `res.added`, which includes the entries just archived.

**A second restore repeats it.** `sftkHistoryMergeBackup` (`sftk-history.js:561`) builds its `have` set from hot ids only, so the archived entries are added again, overflow again, and are reported as restored again.

**One correction to the scenario.** A single backup cannot hold 150 entries, because it is built from the hot list of at most 100. The overflow is still reachable: a 100-entry backup restored into a browser that already holds 60 entries (deployments count toward the cap) archives 60. The overflow is the oldest of the merged list, so it can include entries that were already there, not only restored ones.

**Studio path.** `sftk-history.js:569-572` returns `archived: 0`, but `storageSaveHistory` (`studio-core.js:673-675`) then spills the same overflow to the archive without saying so.
confirmed.fix:
Make the report true rather than building an archive reader.

1. In `sftkHistoryRestoreBackup` (`sftk-history.js:578-581`), after the split, compute how many of the added entries stayed in the list: `const keptIds = new Set(split.keep.map(e => e.id)); const usable = add.filter(e => keptIds.has(e.id)).length` (have `sftkHistoryMergeBackup` return the added ids). Record whether `sftkArchPut` threw, and return `{ added: usable, skipped, archived: split.overflow.length, archiveFailed }`.

2. In `sftk-toolhistory.js:172-175`, say "each with its Undo" only for `res.added` (the entries now in the list). Replace the archive clause with: "the K oldest did not fit (the list keeps 100) and have no Undo here — keep the backup file, clear or undo newer entries, then restore again". If `archiveFailed`, say they were not kept.

confirmed.title: An archived Data Studio tool entry shows an enabled Undo that always answers 'no longer in Activity'
confirmed.scenario: A Picklist Manager or Merge change (kind 'tool', not a Toolkit tab) ages past the 100 cap. In Data Studio > History press 'Show 50 older': the entry is drawn by _histToolCard with a red enabled 'Undo (N steps)' button, because sftkToolUndoState only looks at the entry. Clicking it calls sftkHistoryUndo(id, {}), which searches _history only and gets no o.entry, so the toast says 'This entry is no longer in Activity.' and nothing is undone. Deployment runs loaded from the archive can be rolled back (studio-undo reads _archShown); tool entries cannot.
confirmed.why:
The claim survives; I found no guard anywhere on the path.

1. **Archived tool entries are drawn.** `studio-history.js:1098` loads archive pages into `_archShown` with `_archived: true`. `renderHistory` (`studio-history.js:467`, `483`) merges every `_archShown` entry that is not a Toolkit-tab tool into the list, and `studio-history.js:535` sends `kind === 'tool'` to `_histToolCard`. `SFTK_TOOLKIT_TOOLS` (`sftk-history.js:462-466`) does not list 'Picklist Manager', 'Merge', 'Org Seeder', 'Transfer' or 'Scan & Compare', so those entries stay in Data Studio History. They reach the archive through `storageSaveHistory` (`studio-core.js:669-675`), which moves overflow past 100 to `sftkArchPut` whatever the kind.

2. **The button is enabled.** `_histToolGroups` (`studio-history.js:392-394`) takes its state from `sftkToolUndoState(run)` (`sftk-history.js:200-212`). That function reads only `entry.toolUndo`; it never looks at `_archived` or at whether the entry is in `_history`. An archived entry with steps gets `disabled: false` and a red "Undo (N steps)" button.

3. **The click cannot find the entry.** The delegate at `studio-core.js:874` calls `window.undoTool(arg)` with the id only. `studio-history.js:994` then calls `sftkHistoryUndo(id, {})`. In Data Studio `sftkHistoryAll()` returns `_history` only (`sftk-history.js:195`), and `o.entry` is undefined, so `sftk-history.js:314-316` returns `{ ok: false, text: 'This entry is no longer in Activity.' }`. Nothing is written and the user gets a warning toast.

4. **Deployment runs do handle the archive.** `studio-history.js:405` and `954` both fall back to `_archShown.find(...)`. The `o.entry` hand-in added on 2026-11-17 (`sftk-history.js:310-315`) exists for exactly this case, but `undoTool` does not use it.

No test was run; this is from reading the code.
confirmed.fix:
In `studio-history.js:992-994`, hand the archived entry to the undo:

```js
const held = (_archShown || []).find(r => r && r.id === id && r.kind === 'tool');
const r = await sftkHistoryUndo(id, held ? { entry: held } : {});
```

`sftkHistoryUndo` already accepts `o.entry` (`sftk-history.js:314-315`).

One follow-on: after the undo, `sftkHistoryAppend(entry)` (`sftk-history.js:402`, `178-180`) pushes the archived entry into `_history`. The entry would then be in both `_history` and `_archShown`, so the card could draw twice. Either drop it from `_archShown` once the undo has run, or write it back with `sftkArchPut([held])` as `_sftkUndoPersist` does (`studio-undo.js:130-133`).

confirmed.title: 'Show older' skips archived runs once an old entry has been put back at the end of the hot list
confirmed.scenario: The hot list is full. Undo the oldest hot entry E (or run a long Undo all): the undo's own entry evicts E to the archive, then sftkHistoryAppend(entry) pushes E back at the END of the list. The cap evicts by position, so every later append evicts entries that are newer than E, including deployment runs. In Data Studio > History the bar says 'N older runs archived' and offers 'Show 50 older', but the page asks the archive for runs strictly older than the oldest startedAt on the page, which is E's (Toolkit entries in _history count too, though they are not drawn). The runs archived after E are newer than that bound and are never loaded, so their Roll back and Retry cannot be reached. The same happens after Restore a backup puts old entries into a hot list that has room.
confirmed.why:
The claim survives; I found no guard.

1. **The old entry does go back at the end.** `sftkHistoryUndo` (sftk-history.js:398-402) first ends the undo's own journal, then re-appends the original entry. With a full hot list in Data Studio, the first append pushes the undo entry and `storageSaveHistory` (studio-core.js:668-675) reassigns `_history = split.keep`, archiving index 0, which is E. The second call, `sftkHistoryAppend(entry)` (sftk-history.js:178-179), no longer finds E and does `_history.push(entry)`. The popup path does the same at sftk-history.js:187-190 (`if (at >= 0) list[at] = entry; else list.push(entry)`). The comment at 310-315 confirms the eviction was seen live during Undo all.

2. **The cap evicts by position, not date.** `sftkHistorySplit` (sftk-archive.js:25) keeps `list.slice(-c)`. Nothing re-sorts `_history` after an append; the only sort is in `sftkHistoryMergeBackup`. E, with the oldest `startedAt`, stays in the hot list while every later append archives entries newer than E.

3. **'Show older' is bounded by E.** studio-history.js:1093-1096 takes the minimum `startedAt` over `[..._history, ..._archShown]` and calls `sftkArchList(oldest, 50)`. That uses `IDBKeyRange.upperBound(beforeStartedAt, true)` (sftk-archive.js:81), so only runs strictly older than E come back. Each loaded page only lowers the bound further, so runs archived after E are never reachable.

4. **The bar still advertises them.** `remaining = total - _archShown.length` (studio-history.js:1086) counts the unreachable runs, so the button stays and loads nothing. Their Roll back, Retry and per-run export cannot be reached; only 'Export all' (null bound, line 1108) sees them.

The 'Restore a backup' variant is weaker: `sftkHistoryMergeBackup` (sftk-history.js:564) sorts by `startedAt`, so restored old entries sit at the front and are evicted first. It only bites if the archive already holds newer runs while the hot list has room (after the quota spill at studio-core.js:683). The undo scenario alone is enough to confirm the defect.

Not run; this is from reading the code.

confirmed.title: 'Export all (incl. archive)' writes the stale archived copy of an entry that is also in the hot list
confirmed.scenario: An entry is evicted to the archive before its undo is recorded (the case sftkHistoryUndo's o.entry fallback exists for: Undo all on a long run, or an undo of the oldest hot entry), then re-appended to the hot list with toolUndo.done. The archive keeps the earlier copy under the same id, without done. The audit export takes every archive row first and drops the hot row with the same id, so the file reports that change as not undone, while the undo's own entry in the same file says it was. The 'N older runs archived' count also includes these duplicates.
confirmed.evidence:
studio-history.js 1108-1110: const arch = await sftkArchList(null, 1e9); const archIds = new Set(arch.map(h => h.id)); const entries = [...arch, ..._history.filter(h => !archIds.has(h.id))]
sftk-history.js 401-402: entry.toolUndo.done = {...}; await sftkHistoryAppend(entry);  (writes the hot list only; the archived copy is not updated or deleted)
confirmed.why:
The claim survives; no guard was found.

**How the duplicate id arises**
- `sftk-history.js:398` — `sftkHistoryEnd(j, …)` appends the undo's own entry first. In Data Studio that goes through `storageSaveHistory` (`studio-core.js:668-675`): `sftkHistorySplit(_history, 100)`, `_history = split.keep`, `sftkArchPut(split.overflow)`. With the hot list at the cap, the oldest entry is archived without `toolUndo.done`. If the entry being undone is the oldest hot one, it is that entry.
- `sftk-history.js:401-402` — `entry.toolUndo.done = {...}; await sftkHistoryAppend(entry);`. In `sftkHistoryAppend` (`sftk-history.js:178-179`) `findIndex` returns -1 and the entry is pushed to the end of `_history`. It is the newest element, so the split keeps it hot.
- The popup path does the same (`sftk-history.js:187-191`), and `_historyAdoptToolUpdates(..., true)` at `studio-core.js:641` then pushes the entry into Studio's `_history`.
- The `o.entry` fallback (`sftk-history.js:314-315`, passed by `sftkHistoryUndoMany` at line 445) gives the same result for an entry archived earlier in an Undo all.
- Nothing updates or deletes the archived row: `sftk-archive.js` only has put, list, count, delete-older-than and clear. The row is overwritten only when the entry overflows a second time, about 100 entries later.

**Why the export picks the stale copy**
- `studio-history.js:1108-1110` — `archIds` is built from every archive row and `_history.filter(h => !archIds.has(h.id))` drops the hot copy, which is the one carrying `done`.
- `histExportPayload` (`studio-history.js:278`) spreads `...e`, so the file shows that change with `toolUndo.steps` and no `done`. The undo's own entry in the same file has `undoOf` pointing at it.

**Count**
- `sftkArchCount` (`studio-history.js:1083`, `sftk-archive.js:68`) is a plain `st.count()`, so the "N older runs archived" figure includes the duplicate row.

**Trigger**
With at least 100 entries in Activity, undo the oldest hot entry (or run Undo all on a long list), then click "Export all (incl. archive)".

Not run; this is from reading the code.
confirmed.fix:
In `studio-history.js:1109-1110`, let the hot copy win:

```js
const hotIds = new Set(_history.map(h => h.id));
const entries = [...arch.filter(h => !hotIds.has(h.id)), ..._history]
```

(the `.sort(...)` that follows stays as it is).

Optional, for the count: subtract the archive rows whose id is in `_history` from `total` in the archive bar, or delete the archived row when an entry is re-appended to the hot list.

confirmed.title: A rule or flow that was switched off or re-versioned after the page read its list is switched ON (or back to the old version) when the run ends
confirmed.scenario: The rule and flow lists are read once when the Deploy page opens and never again for the same target and objects. Open the page with rule R active and ticked (or 'pause validation rules' checked). Deactivate R by hand in Setup, as someone preparing a load might. Press Deploy. Hydrate reads R's Metadata with active:false and ignores it; the switch to OFF 'verifies' (already off); at the end the run PATCHes active:true. R ends up ON although it was OFF before the run. Flows behave the same: the cached `version` (say v3) is written back as activeVersionNumber even if v4 was activated, or the flow deactivated, after the page opened.
confirmed.evidence:
studio-deploy.js 2361: `const list = await sftkVrPauseList(sess, objects, undefined, { light: true });` (the Active = true filter is applied only at this moment)
studio-deploy.js 2372 / 2310: reload only when key differs
sftk-vrpause.js 98-100: hydrate stores rec.Metadata without looking at Metadata.active
sftk-vrpause.js 191: `ok: isOn === wantOn` (already off counts as switched off, so it lands in pausedR.off and is switched ON by sftkVrPauseOn)
sftk-flowpause.js 106: `body: { Metadata: { activeVersionNumber: wantOn ? f.version : 0 } }`
confirmed.why:
The claim survives; I found no guard anywhere on the path.

**The list is read once and never refreshed.**
- `studio-deploy.js:2372` (rules) and `:2310` (flows) reload only when `!_dep*Pause.on || key !== key`. The key is `${p.targetOrg}|${objects.join(',')}` (2352, 2286).
- `_depRulePause` and `_depFlowPause` are module-level and are assigned only inside `load()` (2356, 2291). A grep finds no other reset, so the list lives as long as the Studio tab keeps the same target and objects.

**Rules: nothing between Deploy and the write re-checks Active.**
- `_depReconcile` (2410-2414) takes `vpAll.rules` straight from the cached list.
- `beforeWrites` (2429) calls `sftkVrPauseHydrate`, which stores `rec.Metadata` without looking at `Metadata.active` (`sftk-vrpause.js:98-100`).
- `_sftkVpSwitch` PATCHes `{...md, active:false}` and its verify is `ok: isOn === wantOn` (`sftk-vrpause.js:191`). A rule that is already off passes, lands in `r.done`, and comes back as `pausedR.off` (225).
- `resumeR` (`studio-deploy.js:2420`) then calls `sftkVrPauseOn`, which PATCHes `active:true` (`sftk-vrpause.js:256`, body at 165).
- Result: a rule deactivated in Setup after the page opened ends the run ON. The same rule is also written to `sftk_vr_run_paused` (209), so a closed tab offers to switch it on from the leftover card.

**Flows: the cached version is written back unchecked.**
- `version` is captured only in `sftkFlowPauseList` (`sftk-flowpause.js:71-75`) at page load.
- `sftkFlowPauseOff` writes `activeVersionNumber: 0`; its verify (115-118) only checks `!!ActiveVersionId === wantOn`, so an already-inactive flow counts as switched off.
- `sftkFlowPauseOn` writes `activeVersionNumber: f.version` (106). If v4 was activated after the page opened, the flow is put back to v3. If the flow was deactivated, it is re-activated at v3.
- The switch-back verify also only checks that some version is active, so the log reports "back ON at v3 — verified".

**What does not prevent it.** `runReconcile` (`studio-reconcile.js:3045-3047`) only calls `beforeWrites`; it does no re-read. The confirmation dialog lists the stale names but gives no sign that their state changed.

I did not run this against an org (read-only review); the trace is from the code alone.
confirmed.fix:
Re-read the state just before the switch, inside the two `beforeWrites` hooks in `studio-deploy.js`, and act only on what is still active.

**Rules (`_depReconcile`, before line 2429):**
1. Call `sftkVrPauseList(sess, [...written], undefined, { light: true })` again.
2. Keep only the `vp.rules` whose `id` is still in that fresh Active = true list. Log the dropped ones as "already off — left as it is".
3. Hydrate and call `sftkVrPauseOff` on the kept rules only. If none are left, return `true` without switching anything.

A belt-and-braces addition in `sftkVrPauseHydrate`: drop a rule whose `rec.Metadata.active === false` (or whose packaged xml has `<active>false</active>`) instead of keeping it.

**Flows (`_depRun`, before line 2492):**
1. Call `sftkFlowPauseList(sess, objects)` again.
2. For each `fp.flows` entry, find the fresh row by `apiName`. Drop the flow if it is absent (now inactive); otherwise overwrite `f.version` with the fresh version.
3. Call `sftkFlowPauseOff` on the remaining flows only.

Both changes cost one or two queries per run and close the window down to the few seconds between the re-read and the switch.

confirmed.title: A dry run bypasses duplicate rules on every object, while the real run bypasses only the objects ticked in the pause panel

Dry run of Accounts that match an Alert duplicate rule: the dry run is started with no dupePause, and the probe composite takes the bypass header with no object, so allowSave=true goes on the whole transaction. confirmed.title: Dry run packs up to 24 sObject Collections subrequests into one composite; Salesforce documents a limit of 5 per composite request
confirmed.scenario: Dry run of a deployment tree with 6 or more object nodes that reach a write (e.g. Account > Contact, Opportunity, Case, Asset, Contract). sftkProbeCompositeBody emits one composite/sobjects subrequest per node plus the poison, and the guard only refuses above maxSubs = 24. The REST Composite resource allows 25 subrequests but only 5 of them may be sObject Collections or query operations, so Salesforce should refuse the whole request with HTTP 400. sfProbeComposite throws, the user sees "dry run stopped: HTTP 400 ..." and every record is counted "not reached", while the code's own limit line promises 24 levels. The claim survives on the code; the Salesforce limit itself is from the documentation as I remember it, not run against an org.

- **Only guard is 24:** background.js:3137 refuses only when `probeSubs.length > PL.maxSubs`, and `maxSubs` is 24 (background.js:1235). Nothing else caps or splits the subrequests before `sfProbeComposite` at background.js:3148.

The Composite resource documentation allows 25 subrequests, of which at most 5 may be sObject Collections or query operations. So a tree with 6 to 24 writing nodes passes the guard and should be refused whole by Salesforce.

I found no evidence in the repository that a dry run with more than 5 subrequests was ever run live: no test, doc or handover note mentions this limit or a 6-level run. `test/dryrun-probe-1103.test.mjs` only checks the body shape.
confirmed.fix: In `sftkProbeLimits()` (background.js:1235) set `maxSubs: 5` and correct the comment to say a composite takes at most 5 sObject Collections subrequests, plus the poison, which is a plain sObject POST and does not count. confirmed.title: Dry run ignores the per-object duplicate-rule choice: one bypass header for the whole composite

- background.js:3148 is the only probe call site: `sfProbeComposite(tgtOrgUrl, tgtSid, sftkProbeCompositeBody(sending, API_VERSION))`. Nothing after it re-evaluates duplicate rules per object.
- Real writes are per object: background.js:5173 `_runDupHeaders(objectType)`, 5871 and 5990 `_runDupHeaders(records[0].attributes.type)`.
- A partial set is reachable from the UI: studio-deploy.js:2269-2275 `_depDupePauseOpts` returns `objects: sftkPauseDupeObjects(l.rules, _depPauseSkip, written)`; studio-reconcile.js:2553 accepts it as `_dp`; studio-reconcile.js:3313-3315 sets `pushProfile.probe = true` and `pushProfile.dupBypassObjects = _dp.objects` on the same profile; background.js:1402-1403 turns that into the Set.

If the outer header applies to subrequests, the dry run reports the Contact "would be written" and the real Deploy then refuses it with DUPLICATES_DETECTED. If it does not apply, the dry run refuses the ticked Account rows that the real run would write. The comment at 1390-1391 ("rides along exactly as on a real write") is not true for a per-object choice.

Send the header per subrequest instead of on the outer call.

1. background.js `sftkProbeCompositeBody(subs, apiVersion, hdrFor)`: for each subrequest compute `const h = hdrFor ? hdrFor(s.objType) : null;` and add `...(h && Object.keys(h).length ? { httpHeaders: h } : {})` to the subrequest object. 2. background.js:3148: call `sftkProbeCompositeBody(sending, API_VERSION, o => _runDupHeaders(o))`.
3. background.js:1395: drop `..._runDupHeaders()` from the outer request headers, so an unticked object cannot inherit a bypass.

confirmed.title: Sweep rows of the previous field can be appended to the next field's scan while the join is still looking up ids
confirmed.scenario: A sweep of field A ends with many code hits; _sweepJoin runs one Tooling query per item in sequence. Meanwhile the user picks field B and scans it. resetFieldAndBelow nulls _orgSweep and _lastScan, the scan then sets _lastScan to B's. _sweepJoin has no check between awaits: when its loop ends it executes _lastScan.deps = [..._lastScan.deps, ...rows] on B's scan (rows carry RefMetadataComponentName of A). _sweepRun returns on _orgSweep !== s without drawing, so the rows surface on B's next redraw (a filter click) as fixable rows of B. If the scan has not finished yet, _lastScan is null and the line throws an unhandled TypeError instead. The Tooling lookups also use the live _orgUrl/_sid, so after an org switch they resolve names in the new org.
confirmed.evidence:
if (rows.length) _lastScan.deps = [..._lastScan.deps, ...rows];
return rows.length;
confirmed.why:
The claim holds; no guard exists inside _sweepJoin.

C:\Users\yonas\OneDrive\Desktop\Saleforce Toolkit\field-cleaner.js:
- 3870-3896 `_sweepJoin(s)`: checks `!_lastScan` only once at entry (3871), then awaits one Tooling `SF_QUERY` per fresh Apex class/trigger/page/component/LWC hit (3884; `sftkSweepIdQuery` in sftk-sweep.js:723-729 returns a query for exactly those kinds). Nothing after an await compares `_orgSweep === s`, the field, or the scan it started with. Line 3894 then runs `if (rows.length) _lastScan.deps = [..._lastScan.deps, ...rows];` against whatever the module-level `_lastScan` is at that moment.
- 1306-1311 `resetFieldAndBelow()` (called on field/object pick at 1043 and 1244, and on org change at 823) sets `_lastScan = null; _orgSweep = null`. The comment at 823 says "their loops stop on it", but the join's loop does not.
- 2140-2141: the next scan assigns a fresh `_lastScan` for field B.
- 4042-4043: the caller's `if (_orgSweep !== s) return;` comes after `await _sweepJoin(s)`, so it only skips the redraw; the mutation has already happened.

Two outcomes, by timing:
1. Join ends while `_lastScan` is null (user picked another field or object and B's scan has not finished): line 3894 throws a TypeError on `null.deps`, an unhandled rejection out of `_sweepRun`. One in-flight lookup that resolves to a row is enough. Nothing is corrupted; the abandoned sweep just dies in the console.
2. Join ends after B's scan has set `_lastScan`: rows built with `RefMetadataComponentName` of field A (`field` is captured at 3872 before the awaits) and `_sweep: true` are appended to B's deps and appear on B's next `renderResults(_lastScan.deps, ...)` as fixable rows. This needs the join to outlast B's whole scan, so it takes many fresh code hits or slow Tooling answers. I did not trace what the row actions then do with such a row.

The org-switch part is also literally true (3884 reads live `_orgUrl`/`_sid`), with the same null-or-foreign `_lastScan` consequence.

Not run; established by reading the code only.
confirmed.fix:
In `_sweepJoin`, capture the scan at entry and bail if the sweep or scan was replaced:

`const scan = _lastScan;` after the 3871 guard; after the `await bg(...)` at 3884 add `if (_orgSweep !== s || _lastScan !== scan) return 0;`; and change 3894 to `if (rows.length && _orgSweep === s && _lastScan === scan) scan.deps = [...scan.deps, ...rows];`.

The early return also stops the remaining Tooling lookups from going to a newly selected org.

refuted.title: Every file of every retrieve is kept in memory until the last retrieve lands

- The claim itself says "Plausible, not measured". It gives no org size, byte count or observed crash.

If hardening is wanted anyway, it is cheap. The grep loop is strictly per file with no cross-file state (sftk-sweep.js:638-658). The background half of the claim is accurate: sfMetadataSoap (background.js:4919-4942) puts the caller's sid into the SOAP header, uses plain sfFetch, and returns a fault as { error } rather than throwing SESSION_EXPIRED, so neither handleMessage's retry (3766) nor field-cleaner's bg() refresh (field-cleaner.js:873-876) can fire.

The scenario still cannot happen, because the page's sid is refreshed by a different path that the claim missed:

1. A re-login writes a new sid cookie. background.js:6289-6296 (chrome.cookies.onChanged) broadcasts SF_SESSION_REFRESHED for any non-removed sid cookie on a Salesforce domain.
2. Field Cleaner is loaded only in popup.html (line 377). popup.js:818-826 handles that message by calling initSession('cookie_changed').
3. initSession (popup.js:662-690) hides every tab, reads a fresh session, assigns the globals orgUrl/sid (685-686) and renders the home page. The Field Cleaner view is no longer on screen.
4. Re-opening Field Cleaner runs initFieldCleanerTab (popup.js:3308-3310), which calls FieldCleaner.updateSession(orgUrl, sid) unconditionally. That sets _sid (field-cleaner.js:838-841), and every SF_MD_* call reads _sid at call time.

- Line 1123-1124: the Start query has no expiry filter and LIMIT 1, so an expired foreign USER_DEBUG flag is picked up.

A one-line hardening would be `if ((dn || !stored) && sftkDbgPriorLive(ex, Date.now()))` at line 1150, plus `sftkDbgPriorLive(tf.prior, Date.now())` when building `restore` at line 1301 for the case where the foreign expiry passes mid-trace.
